comment: Mode S reply (ADS-B extended squitter): the 5-bit downlink format decides the length, 56 bits (DF 0-15) or 112 (DF 16-31), the last 24 of which are the parity over everything before them. Out comes what is between the DF and the parity (the 27 or 83 bits of fields: for DF 17 capability, ICAO address and the 56-bit message). DF 11 and the surveillance replies overlay an address on the parity, so only replies whose parity is clean pass (DF 17 / 18)
